A file picture of the banni festival at Devaragattu in Kurnool district. File | Photo Credit: U. Subramanyam
All arrangements have been made for the annual ‘banni’ festival , popularly known as ‘karrala samaram , at Devaragattu in Holagunda mandal of the district on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) night. People from three villages vie with each other to snatch the idol of the presiding deity, Sri Mala Malleswara Swamy, resulting in injuries, sometimes even fatal ones.
Superintendent of Police Vikrant Patil asked the villagers not to resort to violence in the name of following tradition and said strict measures were taken to curb the sale of illicit liquor and country-made liquor. Bind-over proceedings were initiated against more than 190 individuals, he said.
To prevent villagers from clashing, the police seize sticks from neighbouring villages, and this time too more than 300 sticks have been seized during 40 cordon and search operations.
Five check-posts and 10 police pickets have been set up and continuous surveillance has been put using 110 night-vision CCTV cameras, 700 LED lights, and 10 drone cameras.
“Tight security arrangements are in place and a total of 1,000 police personnel, including Additional SPs, DSPs, circle inspectors, and sub-inspectors were roped in for bandobust to ensure that no untoward incidents occur,” the SP said.
దేవరగట్టు బన్ని ఉత్సవానికి 1,000 మంది పోలీసులతో పటిష్ట భద్రతా ఏర్పాట్లు చేపట్టినట్లు కర్నూలు ఎస్పీ శ్రీ విక్రాంత్ పాటిల్ తెలిపారు. సీసీటీవీ నిఘా ఏర్పాటు చేశాం. భక్తులు ప్రశాంతంగా సంప్రదాయబద్ధంగా ఉత్సవంలో పాల్గొనాలి. #APPOLICE100 #AndhraPradeshPolice #PoliceKurnool #APPolice https://t.co/gdTmYojLt8
Mr. Patil said two district-level meetings, one at the Kurnool Collectorate and another at Devaragattu, were held in coordination with the district administration to review the arrangements and security measures for the festival.
Special awareness meetings were conducted in villages surrounding Devaragattu such as Neraniki, Neraniki Thanda, Kothapeta, Arikera and Ellarthi to sensitise the local population. Individuals with a history of involvement in conflicts, as well as those engaged in the sale of illicit liquor, have been identified and bound over, he said.
